title: Circular Letter DHCQ 20-3-700: Schedule II-VI acute-use medications in hospice inpatient facilities
rule_summary: Department of Public Health Circular Letter DHCQ 20-3-700 (March 6, 2020), jointly issued by the Bureau of Health Care Safety and Quality and the Board of Registration in Pharmacy through the Bureau of Health Professions Licensure, outlines a process through which an inpatient hospice facility's pharmacy provider is permitted to store certain non-patient specific medications on-site at the hospice facility for patient administration. It attaches a list of Schedule II-VI controlled substances that hospice inpatient facilities, as defined in 105 CMR 141.000, may allow a pharmacy to store on their premises via an automated dispensing device (ADD) for acute use, meaning medications intended to treat patient symptoms that are not life threatening but require use in a timely manner to provide prompt palliative care; the supply should only be enough to treat the patient until the pharmacy can fill and deliver the full prescription. The pharmacy provider must use an ADD to store and secure acute use medications, must obtain a machine-specific Controlled Substance Registration from the Board of Registration in Pharmacy, and must determine whether a machine-specific DEA number is required; in addition to continuous monitoring by video, other ADD requirements are in Board Policy 2019-02. An ADD at an inpatient hospice facility may contain up to, but not more than, the allowed quantity for each category, per facility and based on licensed bed capacity: analgesics (CII-CV) 50 units for <10 beds, 100 for 11-20 beds and 150 for >21 beds; sedatives/anticonvulsants (CII-CV) 30, 60 and 90; ancillary medications (CVI, e.g. antiemetics, antipsychotics) 25, 50 and 75. Facilities are not required to have all items or the maximum quantity; each facility should develop its own formulary with the pharmacy providing the on-site ADD and develop policies and procedures, including controlled substance accountability and security measures, subject to review. The contents of the ADD remain the property of the pharmacy until dispensed for administration pursuant to a prescriber's prescription or order; medications dispensed through the ADD must be reconciled by the pharmacy with prescriptions; and each unit must be tamper evident/resistant, in an individually packaged, single dose form. The facility's acute use practices, policies and procedures may be reviewed at any time by Bureau of Health Care Safety and Quality or Board staff.
exam_relevance: Tests the purpose limit of hospice acute-use stock, the pharmacy's machine-specific registration and DEA determination, pharmacy ownership until dispensing, reconciliation, and the three category caps by bed band.

common_confusions: Acute use means symptoms that are not life threatening but need timely palliation; the supply bridges only until the pharmacy fills and delivers the full prescription.
The ADD contents belong to the pharmacy until dispensed for administration, and the pharmacy reconciles them with prescriptions.
The printed bands are <10, 11-20 and >21 beds; the list does not print a band for exactly 10 or exactly 21 beds.
